function.name: sandbox
function.description: Run code and commands in a temporary isolated E2B Linux sandbox for this WhatsApp user. One sandbox is reused across turns until you kill it or it times out. Call this for executing Python/JS/TS/R/Java/Bash, installing packages, reading/writing files, starting servers, or exposing a public URL. Pick an action. Auto-creates a sandbox when needed.

action.description: Sub-tool to run. create: start a new sandbox. connect: reconnect by sandboxId. info: sandbox details. kill: destroy it. set_timeout: extend lifetime. run_code: execute code (python, javascript, typescript, r, java, bash). run_command: shell command. list_processes: running processes. kill_process: kill by pid. files_list, files_read, files_write, files_mkdir, files_remove, files_rename, files_exists, files_info: filesystem. download: copy a sandbox file and send it on WhatsApp. get_url: public https URL for a port. install: install packages with pip or npm.

sandboxId.description: Existing sandbox id. Used by connect, or to reuse a known sandbox.

template.description: Optional E2B template name or id when creating a sandbox. Default is the code-interpreter template.

timeoutMs.description: Sandbox lifetime in milliseconds from now. Default 300000 (5 minutes).

language.description: Language for run_code: python, javascript, typescript, r, java, bash. Default python.

command.description: Shell command for run_command, for example ls -la or python3 -m http.server 3000

cwd.description: Working directory for run_command or run_code context.

background.description: If true, start run_command in the background and return the pid.

path.description: Absolute sandbox path for filesystem actions. Default /home/user.

files.description: Multiple files for files_write. Each item has path and content.

depth.description: Directory listing depth for files_list. Default 1.

port.description: Sandbox port to expose with get_url, for example 3000.

packages.description: Package names for install, for example numpy, pandas, axios.

manager.description: Package manager for install: pip or npm. Default pip.
